culture.textEn: {ko:을} and {ko:를} mark the thing an action is done to. The word before them decides which: {ko:을} after a final consonant, {ko:를} after a vowel.

sources.title: 문법(文法)
sources.publisher: Academy of Korean Studies, Encyclopedia of Korean Culture
sources.quoteOrLocator: 내용, (2)접사의 모습 ① 곡용접사 단락: 목적격 을/를을 조사로 들고, 체언 어기의 받침 유무에 따라 조사가 두 형태로 갈라진다고 설명하며 그 예를 학생이·은·을…(받침 있는 말 아래)와 학교가·는·를…(받침 없는 말 아래)로 나열한다.

sources.title: 을
sources.publisher: National Institute of Korean Language, Standard Korean Language Dictionary
sources.quoteOrLocator: 표제어 을 2 「조사」 1 「1」 뜻풀이: 동작이 직접 미치는 대상을 나타내는 격 조사로 풀이함. 같은 항목은 받침이 있는 체언 다음에 붙는다고 표시하고 참고 어휘로 를을 든다.

verification.notes: Line 1 (passes: 1, author sourcing, 2026-10-14): the claim is that 을 and 를 mark the object of an action and that the choice follows the word before them, 을 after a final consonant and 를 after a vowel. Encyclopedia of Korean Culture, 문법, the 곡용접사 paragraph, names 을/를 as the object case particle and says a particle splits into two forms by whether the stem has a final consonant (학생을 against 학교를); the Standard Korean Language Dictionary, 을 2 sense 1, defines it as the case particle for the direct target of an action. Both pages resolved (HTTP 200) on 2026-10-14. The note is an English paraphrase; the locators are Korean summaries, not quotations. Backs the q1 and q3 pattern notes and every particle round of the Sentence Builder. Line 2 (passes: 2, independent fact check, pass 2b, 2026-10-14): a session that did not author the cell fetched both sources again (HTTP 200). Encyclopedia of Korean Culture, 문법, (2) 접사의 모습, ① 곡용접사: confirmed. It lists 을/를 as the object case marker and says the particle takes one of two forms by whether the stem ends in a final consonant, with 학생을 against 학교를. The Standard Korean Language Dictionary, 을 2, sense 1, defines it as the case particle for the direct target of an action: confirmed. The locator claimed that the 를 entry appears on the same results page with the same definition. That is false: the 을 results page lists only 을 1, 을 2 and -을 3. The locator now cites what the 을 2 entry itself shows (it attaches after a noun ending in a consonant and lists 를 as a related word). Note text unchanged. No run of words is shared between the note and either source; each locator shares at most a section heading or a few dictionary terms with its source page. Line 3 (passes: 3, MAR culture review, pass 5, 2026-10-14): both sources fetched again (HTTP 200). Encyclopedia of Korean Culture, 문법, ① 곡용접사: 을/를 as the object case marker, two forms by a final consonant (학생을 against 학교를): confirmed. Standard Korean Language Dictionary, 을 2 (word_no 469161, entry view): 「조사」 1 is marked for use after a noun with a final consonant, sense 「1」 is the case particle for the direct target of an action, and 를 is listed under 참고 어휘: confirmed. The source link now opens the entry view instead of the results page, which shows only sense 「1」. The bare 1 in the locator is the entry's own sense-group number and stays. Note text unchanged; no run of words shared with either locator. Locator precision (MAR re-review, 2026-10-14): the 곡용접사 paragraph prints the forms as lists (학생이·은·을… and 학교가·는·를…), read as 학생+을 and 학교+를; the locator now cites those lists rather than the words 학생을 and 학교를, which the page does not spell out. Note text unchanged.

culture.textEn: {ko:싶어요} after an action word ending in {ko:고} says that you want to do it: {ko:하고} {ko:싶어요}, I want to do it.

sources.title: 싶다
sources.publisher: National Institute of Korean Language, Standard Korean Language Dictionary
sources.quoteOrLocator: 표제어 싶다 「보조 형용사」 「1」 뜻풀이: 동사 뒤 -고 싶다 꼴로 쓰여, 앞말이 나타내는 행동을 하려는 마음이나 욕구이 있음을 나타냄(요약).

sources.title: 보조용언(補助用言)
sources.publisher: Academy of Korean Studies, Encyclopedia of Korean Culture
sources.quoteOrLocator: 내용: 보조용언은 본용언 뒤에 정해진 어미를 취한다는 단락(예 먹고 싶다)과, 보조형용사 목록의 첫 항목 바람(希望)으로 싶다를 든 부분.

verification.notes: Line 1 (passes: 1, author sourcing, 2026-10-14): the claim is that 싶어요 after a verb in -고 expresses wanting to do that action. The Standard Korean Language Dictionary, 싶다 (auxiliary adjective) sense 1, defines it as expressing the wish to do what the preceding word describes; the Encyclopedia of Korean Culture, 보조용언, says an auxiliary takes a fixed ending on the main verb (its example 먹고 싶다) and lists 싶다 first among auxiliary adjectives under 바람 (wish). Both pages resolved (HTTP 200) on 2026-10-14. English paraphrase only; locators are Korean summaries. Backs the q1 pattern note and the Hoya lines about what we want to play. Line 2 (passes: 2, independent fact check, pass 2b, 2026-10-14): a session that did not author the cell fetched both sources again (HTTP 200). The Standard Korean Language Dictionary, 싶다, auxiliary adjective, sense 1, marks the use after a verb in the -고 싶다 pattern and defines it as having the wish to do what the preceding word describes: confirmed. The locator now names the -고 싶다 pattern, which is the part of the entry that backs the -고 in the note. Encyclopedia of Korean Culture, 보조용언, 내용: the main verb takes a fixed ending before an auxiliary (example 먹고 싶다), and 싶다 is listed first among auxiliary adjectives under 바람 (希望): confirmed. Note text unchanged. No run of words is shared between the note and either source; each locator shares at most a few dictionary terms with its source page. Line 3 (passes: 3, MAR culture review, pass 5, 2026-10-14): both sources fetched again (HTTP 200). Standard Korean Language Dictionary, 싶다 (word_no 455652, entry view), 「보조 형용사」 「1」: used after a verb in the -고 싶다 pattern for the wish to do that action: confirmed. Encyclopedia of Korean Culture, 보조용언: the main verb takes a fixed ending before the auxiliary (먹고 싶다), and 싶다 is listed under 바람: confirmed. The dictionary link now opens the entry view. Note text unchanged; no run of words shared with either locator. Locator precision (MAR re-review, 2026-10-14): the locator now uses the entry's own term 욕구 (마음이나 욕구) instead of 바람. Note text unchanged.

culture.textEn: {ko:에} after a place, with a going word like {ko:가요}, marks where you are headed: {ko:공원에} {ko:가요}, I go to the park.

sources.title: 격(格)
sources.publisher: Academy of Korean Studies, Encyclopedia of Korean Culture
sources.quoteOrLocator: 내용, 격의 종류를 차례로 설명하는 단락: 부사격조사로 에, 에게 등을 들고, 부사격이 뜻으로 처소나 지향점 따위를 나타낸다고 설명한 부분.

sources.title: 에
sources.publisher: National Institute of Korean Language, Standard Korean Language Dictionary
sources.quoteOrLocator: 표제어 에 4 「조사」 1 「3」 뜻풀이: 앞말을 나아가는 방향의 부사어로 만드는 격 조사로 풀이하고, 용례로 학교에 가다와 지금 산에 간다를 든다.

verification.notes: Line 1 (passes: 1, author sourcing, 2026-10-14): the claim is that 에 after a place word marks the place you are going to, as in 공원에 가요. The Encyclopedia of Korean Culture, 격, names 에 among the adverbial case particles and says that case marks a place or a goal (지향점); the Standard Korean Language Dictionary, 에 4 sense 1, defines 에 as the case particle that makes the word before it a place adverbial. Both pages resolved (HTTP 200) on 2026-10-14. English paraphrase only; locators are Korean summaries. Backs the q2 pattern note. Line 2 (passes: 2, independent fact check, pass 2b, 2026-10-14): a session that did not author the cell fetched both sources again (HTTP 200). Encyclopedia of Korean Culture, 격, 내용: 에 is listed among the adverbial case particles, and adverbial case is said to mark a location or a goal (지향점): confirmed. The locator now says this is the paragraph that goes through the kinds of case, because the article has no heading named for it. The Standard Korean Language Dictionary, 에 4, sense 1, defines 에 for a location adverbial (where something is), not a destination. That locator did not back the claim, so it now cites sense 3 of the same entry: the case particle for the direction of movement, with examples such as going to school and going to the mountain. Sense 3 is what supports 공원에 가요. Note text unchanged. No run of words is shared between the note and either source; each locator shares at most a few dictionary terms with its source page. Line 3 (passes: 3, MAR culture review, pass 5, 2026-10-14): both sources fetched again (HTTP 200). Encyclopedia of Korean Culture, 격: 에 among the adverbial case particles, marking a place or a goal (지향점): confirmed. Standard Korean Language Dictionary, 에 4 (word_no 460139, entry view), 「조사」 1 「3」: the case particle for the direction of movement, with 학교에 가다 and 지금 산에 간다 as examples: confirmed; the results page shows only sense 「1」 (location), so the link now opens the entry view. Finding applied: 에 also marks where something is (sense 「1」), so the note now ties the destination reading to a going word ({ko:가요}). Sense 「3」 backs the revised text exactly; no run of words shared with either locator. Locator precision (MAR re-review, 2026-10-14): the locator now gives the entry's second example in full, 지금 산에 간다. Note text unchanged.

notes: Language passes 4, 6, re-review (MAR): spelling, spacing, 해요체, marks and romanization clean; ko glosses are short definitions with no echo; q1 particle rounds test 을 and 를; step titles match the shipped overlays; the read Check keeps the shipped reading-round shape (spec 3.4). Order-it rounds may join two taught patterns. Scored reads assume Word Builder symbols; U-4 checks this once S2-1 ships.

Culture pass 5 and re-review (MAR): no culture claim (section 3.9); n1-n3 re-checked against all six sources, n3 tied to a going word, dictionary links on the entry views, locators in the pages' own wording; traditional and everyday games mixed evenly; no real person, shop, brand or price; no age wording.
